It is designed to be easily consumable by AI systems for analysis, code review,

# Backend Operator Surface

## Purpose

This document maps operator backend behavior to ABI surfaces and the `.operator` runbook. Operator endpoints are for inspection, calldata preparation, incident tracking, and audit evidence. Privileged execution must follow the governance path for the environment.

## Operator Reads

Primary ABI: `IMarketEngine` at the MarketEngine proxy.

- `getOperatorGlobalView()`
- `getOperatorTemplateView(templateId)`
- `getEpochView(templateId, epochId)`
- `getTemplateYieldView(templateId)`
- `getMarketView(templateId)`
- `getRollingLifecycle(templateId)`
- `unreconciledRecoveredByTemplate(templateId)`
- `templates(templateId)`
- `ledgers(templateId)`
- `epochs(templateId, epochId)`

Dispatcher-specific reads:

- `getSelectorModule(selector)`
- `isRootOwnedSelector(selector)`
- `isModuleApproved(module)`
- `isModuleCodeHashAllowed(codeHash)`
- `getModuleCodeHash(module)`
- `proxiableUUID()`

## Operator Action Map

| Category | ABI | Functions | Execution path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pause and config | `IMarketEngine` / dispatcher | `pauseProgram`, `setTreasury`, `setWorkerAuthority`, `setDepositExecutor` | Safe/operator wallet |
| Market setup | `IMarketEngine` | `upsertTemplate`, `initializeMarket` | Safe/operator wallet |
| Manual lifecycle | `IMarketEngine` | `openEpoch`, `lockEpoch`, `resolveEpoch`, `cancelEpoch` | worker/admin wallet or keeper |
| Rolling lifecycle | `IMarketEngine` | `genesisStartRolling`, `genesisLockRolling`, `executeRollingRound`, `haltRollingMarket`, `cancelRollingEpochWhileHalted`, `resetRollingLifecycle` | worker/admin wallet or keeper |
| Yield routing | `IMarketEngine` | `setYieldRouter`, `setLmRewardsEnabled`, `keeperClaimLmRewards`, recovery functions | Safe/operator wallet |
| Oracle admin | `IMarketEngine` | `setRateOracle`, `setSmartDataOracle`, `setMacroOracle`, `setEquityOracle`, `resetOracleCursor` | Safe/operator wallet |
| Fees | `IMarketEngine` | `withdrawFees` | treasury/admin path |
| Module governance | `MarketEngineDispatcher` | `allowModuleCodeHash`, `registerModule`, `revokeModule`, `setSelectorModule` | Safe only |
| Upgrade | `MarketEngineDispatcher` | `upgradeToAndCall` | Safe only |

## Prepared Transaction Endpoint

`POST /api/v1/ops/tx/prepare` should return:

- target address
- chain id
- ABI name
- function signature
- typed args
- encoded calldata
- value
- required role
- runbook reference
- expected events
- post-action validation reads

It should not sign or broadcast governance transactions.

## Live Refresh

Operator endpoints may accept `?live=true` to perform direct chain reads.

Use direct reads for:

- incident evidence capture
- pre-unpause validation
- module/selector verification
- keeper preflight debugging

Default dashboard refresh should come from PostgreSQL projections to preserve public-RPC budget.

## Incident Alignment

Every critical operator event should map into an incident or audit timeline:

- `RollingHalted`
- `YieldRouterDisabled`
- `YieldEmergencyWithdrawn`
- `EmergencyRecoveredBalanceReassigned`
- `OracleCursorReset`
- `ModuleRegistered`
- `ModuleRevoked`
- `SelectorModuleSet`
- `Upgraded`
- reporter post/clear/rotation events

The backend should make it easy to capture:

- latest operator global view
- affected template view
- affected epoch view
- transaction hash
- decoded event payload
- current block number and timestamp

## Safety Rules

- Reject prepared transactions for root-owned selectors routed through module governance.
- Warn when a requested target is implementation or module address instead of proxy.
- Require explicit environment in every operator request.
- Mark Base Sepolia faucet/test-token actions as testnet-only.
- Mark Base mainnet actions as requiring production governance signoff unless the action is an approved keeper action.

# Backend User Surface

## Purpose

This document maps user-facing backend behavior to ABI surfaces. The backend serves indexed state and transaction metadata; the wallet submits transactions.

## Read Model

Serve these from PostgreSQL by default, projected from chain events and periodically reconciled against contract views:

- market list
- current epoch state
- outcome pool state
- user position state
- claimable epochs
- historical epochs
- faucet state on Base Sepolia

Optional direct chain read fallback:

- `getMarketView(templateId)`
- `getActiveEpochView(templateId)`
- `getEpochView(templateId, epochId)`
- `getOutcomeViews(templateId, epochId)`
- `getPositionView(templateId, epochId, user)`
- `getUserEpochs(templateId, user, cursor, size)`
- `getVaultBalances(templateId)`

Direct reads should be rate limited and exposed only when the response includes a freshness reason.

## User Write ABI Map

| Action | ABI | Function | Submitter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approve stake token | `MockERC20` on Base Sepolia, production ERC20 later | `approve(spender, value)` | User wallet |
| Deposit | `IMarketEngine` at proxy | `depositToSide(templateId, epochId, outcomeIndex, amount)` | User wallet |
| Deposit for beneficiary | `IMarketEngine` at proxy | `depositToSideFor(beneficiary, templateId, epochId, outcomeIndex, amount)` | User wallet or approved executor |
| Switch side | `IMarketEngine` at proxy | `switchSide(templateId, epochId, fromOutcome, toOutcome, grossAmount)` | User wallet |
| Claim one epoch | `IMarketEngine` at proxy | `claim(templateId, epochId)` | User wallet |
| Claim many epochs | `IMarketEngine` at proxy | `claimMany(templateId, epochIds)` | User wallet |
| Faucet request | `TokenFaucet` on Base Sepolia | `request(amount)` | User wallet |

The backend may return prepared call data and estimated display values, but it must not custody user keys or broadcast user transactions.

## User API Shapes

Market detail response should include:

- `templateId`
- `slug`
- `assetSymbol`
- `marketType`
- `executionMode`
- `oracleClass`
- `oracleKind`
- `activeEpochId`
- `activeEpoch`
- `outcomes`
- `poolTotals`
- `timing`
- `claimability`
- `dataFreshness`

Position response should include:

- `wallet`
- `templateId`
- `epochId`
- `stakes`
- `totalStake`
- `entryFeesPaid`
- `switchFeesPaid`
- `claimed`
- `pendingClaimAmount`
- `pendingRefundAmount`
- `status`

Claim response should include:

- claimable epoch IDs
- estimated claim amount
- refund mode flag
- already claimed flag
- transaction target and ABI function name

## Event Sources

User state updates come from:

- `PositionDeposited`
- `SideSwitched`
- `Claimed`
- `UserEpochIndexed`
- `EpochOpened`
- `EpochLocked`
- `EpochResolved`
- `EpochCancelled`
- `RollingRoundExecuted`

For Base Sepolia only:

- `TokenFaucet.Minted`
- `MockERC20.Transfer`
- `MockERC20.Approval`

## Frontend Contract Hints

The API should expose enough transaction metadata for frontend simulation:

- chain id
- target address
- ABI name
- function name
- typed args
- required allowance
- current allowance
- stake token decimals
- expected indexed event after success

Do not hide contract reverts behind generic API errors. Preserve known revert/error names where the client can show a useful failure state.

# Backend Architecture Scaffold

## Purpose

The backend is the API and coordination layer for user apps, operator apps, and automation services. It should be implemented as Go services following [`.tecStackPublicRPC.md`](../.tecStackPublicRPC.md), but grounded in the deployed contract registry and ABI map in [`../abi-map.md`](../abi-map.md).

## Service Boundaries

| Service | Responsibility | Chain access |
|---|---|---|
| `retropick-api` | REST, WebSocket, SIWE sessions, operator endpoints | PostgreSQL by default; explicit `live=true` chain reads only. |
| `retropick-index` | Event indexing and canonical state projection | Batched public RPC `eth_getLogs`. |
| `retropick-keeper` | Manual/rolling lifecycle automation | PostgreSQL schedule plus one live preflight before tx. |
| `retropick-alert` | Incidents, alerts, oracle stale checks | PostgreSQL only in normal operation. |
| `retropick-reporter` | TrustedReporter signing/posting | Only when reporter markets are enabled. |

Do not add a backend path that submits user deposits, switches, claims, or approvals. Users submit those directly from their wallet.

## Proposed Go Layout

```text
.dev/backend
├── README.md
├── user/README.md
├── operator/README.md
└── implementation-target/
    ├── cmd/api
    ├── cmd/indexer
    ├── cmd/keeper
    ├── cmd/alert
    ├── cmd/reporter
    └── internal
        ├── config
        ├── contracts
        ├── db
        ├── http
        ├── ws
        ├── auth
        ├── operator
        ├── indexer
        ├── keeper
        └── alerts
```

The `implementation-target` tree is the intended future Go app layout, not a requirement to place Go code under `.dev`. If the real app later lives elsewhere, keep this document as the architectural contract.

## Contract Registry

Backend config should load a generated registry derived from [`../../abi/address.md`](../../abi/address.md).

Required fields:

- environment name
- chain id
- RPC endpoint list
- MarketEngine proxy
- implementation
- stake token
- faucet
- Chainlink-family adapters
- module addresses
- ABI artifact names
- deployment manifest path

Runtime invariant:

- all MarketEngine reads/writes use the proxy address
- `IMarketEngine` is the default ABI for app reads/writes
- `MarketEngineDispatcher` is used for module registry, UUPS/operator checks, and full event ABI

## API Rules

Default reads:

- serve user and operator views from PostgreSQL projections
- include `lastIndexedBlock`, `lastSyncAt`, and data freshness on responses
- allow explicit operator live reads via `?live=true`

Writes:

- user writes are wallet-owned and frontend-submitted
- operator writes should be represented as decoded calldata or Safe transaction drafts unless the service is explicitly a keeper/reporter service
- keeper writes must create a durable DB execution record before broadcasting

## REST Surface

Public:

- `GET /api/v1/health`
- `GET /api/v1/config/contracts`
- `GET /api/v1/markets`
- `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId`
- `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId/epochs`
- `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId/epochs/:epochId`
- `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId/outcomes`
- `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId/oracle`

User:

- `POST /api/v1/auth/nonce`
- `POST /api/v1/auth/verify`
- `DELETE /api/v1/auth/session`
- `GET /api/v1/user/positions`
- `GET /api/v1/user/epochs`
- `GET /api/v1/user/claims`
- `GET /api/v1/user/history`
- `GET /api/v1/user/faucet-state` for Base Sepolia only

Operator:

- `GET /api/v1/ops/global-state`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/templates`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/templates/:templateId/state`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/templates/:templateId/yield`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/templates/:templateId/epochs/:epochId`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/keeper/schedule`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/keeper/executions`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/oracle/health`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/incidents`
- `POST /api/v1/ops/incidents/:id/update`
- `GET /api/v1/ops/audit`
- `POST /api/v1/ops/tx/prepare` for Safe/operator calldata generation

## WebSocket Channels

- `global`
- `market:{templateId}`
- `epoch:{templateId}:{epochId}`
- `oracle:{feedId}`
- `user:{wallet}`
- `ops:keeper`
- `ops:incidents`
- `ops:governance`

All WebSocket messages are downstream notifications of indexed state, not proof that a transaction is final until the indexer marks the block confirmed under the configured finality depth.

## Database Ownership

Backend-owned projections:

- `contracts`
- `templates`
- `epochs`
- `positions`
- `user_epochs`
- `oracle_readings`
- `oracle_health`
- `chain_events`
- `keeper_schedule`
- `keeper_executions`
- `incidents`
- `audit_log`
- `operator_sessions`

Database rows should store raw integer values as strings or numeric/decimal-safe types at API boundaries. Do not coerce token amounts, pools, claim liabilities, or prices to floating point.

## Safety Rules

- Never serve stale state without a freshness indicator.
- Never use implementation or module addresses as normal app entrypoints.
- Never bypass `.operator/.runbook.md` for privileged operational actions.
- Never assume Base mainnet addresses until a mainnet address registry exists.

# Operator Frontend Scaffold

## Purpose

The operator frontend is an internal dashboard aligned with [../../.operator/.runbook.md](../../.operator/.runbook.md). It displays protocol health, keeper state, oracle state, recovery state, and prepared privileged actions.

## Views

| View | Primary data | Critical states |
|---|---|---|
| Global health | `getOperatorGlobalView` projection | paused, yield router disabled, unreconciled recovery, role drift |
| Templates | `getOperatorTemplateView` projections | user ops blocked, unsafe to unpause, rolling halted |
| Epoch detail | `getEpochView` projection | claimable, refund mode, oracle checkpoints, routed principal |
| Keeper schedule | `keeper_schedule`, `keeper_executions` | expired windows, skipped jobs, failed txs |
| Oracle health | `oracle_health`, feed registry | stale feed, heartbeat pressure, cursor reset |
| Recovery | operator views and incidents | unreconciled recovered, routed claims, router disabled |
| Governance/module audit | dispatcher events | module registration, selector mapping, upgrade |
| Incidents | `incidents`, `audit_log` | open critical incident, unresolved action items |

## Always-Visible Header

Show:

- environment
- chain id
- proxy address
- current block and indexer lag
- `globalPaused`
- `yieldRouterDisabled`
- `totalUnreconciledRecovered`
- latest critical alert

## Prepared Actions

Operator UI may prepare but should not silently execute:

- pause/unpause
- initialize market
- open/lock/resolve/cancel manual epoch
- genesis/execute/halt/reset rolling lifecycle
- set oracle adapters
- reset oracle cursor
- withdraw fees
- yield emergency recovery
- module allow/register/route
- upgrade

Prepared action output must include:

- target address
- ABI/function
- decoded args
- encoded calldata
- required role
- expected events
- validation checklist
- production approval requirement

## Live Refresh

Use explicit live refresh buttons for:

- global operator state
- template operator state
- epoch view
- module selector routing
- adapter addresses

Default polling uses API/Postgres projections. Live refresh should be visible as an operator action because it consumes public RPC and may differ from indexed state.

## Critical Banners

Display blocking banners for:

- `globalPaused == true`
- `yieldRouterDisabled == true`
- `totalUnreconciledRecovered > 0`
- any template `unsafeToUnpauseForTemplate == true`
- rolling halted with non-zero halt reason
- unexpected `Upgraded`
- unexpected module or selector event
- stale oracle health for an active template

## Environment Rules

Base Sepolia:

- show faucet/test token utilities
- allow testnet-only operational drills
- label mock token clearly

Base mainnet:

- hide faucet utilities
- require Safe/governance action path labels
- require release-record links before showing go-live readiness
- never imply a mainnet deployment exists until a mainnet address registry is present

# User Frontend Scaffold

## Purpose

The user frontend is a wallet-first market interface. It reads indexed state from the API and submits user transactions directly from the connected wallet.

## Pages

| Page | Data source | Contract actions |
|---|---|---|
| Market list | `GET /api/v1/markets` | none |
| Market detail | `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId`, WS `market:{templateId}` | deposit, switch |
| Epoch history | `GET /api/v1/markets/:templateId/epochs` | claim if claimable |
| Portfolio | `GET /api/v1/user/positions`, `GET /api/v1/user/claims` | claim, claimMany |
| Faucet | `GET /api/v1/user/faucet-state` | `TokenFaucet.request` on Base Sepolia only |

## Components

- `MarketCard`: template summary, active epoch, total pool, timing
- `EpochTimer`: open/lock/resolve countdown and status
- `OutcomePools`: outcome pool sizes, implied probabilities, winner state
- `OracleBadge`: oracle kind/class/feed label and data freshness
- `DepositForm`: allowance check, approve, deposit
- `SwitchForm`: current stake, target outcome, switch amount
- `ClaimButton`: single claim and batch claim states
- `PortfolioTable`: active, claimable, claimed, no-payout positions
- `FaucetPanel`: Base Sepolia-only faucet status and request

## Contract Actions

Use `IMarketEngine` at the proxy:

- `depositToSide(templateId, epochId, outcomeIndex, amount)`
- `depositToSideFor(beneficiary, templateId, epochId, outcomeIndex, amount)`
- `switchSide(templateId, epochId, fromOutcome, toOutcome, grossAmount)`
- `claim(templateId, epochId)`
- `claimMany(templateId, epochIds)`

Use stake token ABI:

- `approve(marketEngineProxy, amount)`
- `allowance(wallet, marketEngineProxy)`
- `balanceOf(wallet)`
- `decimals()`

Use faucet ABI on Base Sepolia:

- `request(amount)`
- `lastMintAt(wallet)`
- `config()`

## Transaction Flow

1. Read indexed market and position state.
2. Check wallet network and connected address.
3. Check stake token balance and allowance.
4. Simulate the contract call where the wallet provider supports simulation.
5. Submit transaction from wallet.
6. Show pending transaction hash.
7. Wait for indexer confirmation through API/WS.
8. Refresh position and market state.

## Error Handling

Known user-facing failure states:

- wrong network
- insufficient token balance
- insufficient allowance
- betting closed
- invalid outcome
- rolling halted
- protocol paused
- already claimed
- nothing to claim
- stale UI state waiting for indexer

Do not present backend state as final until the indexed block is confirmed under the configured finality depth.

# Frontend Architecture Scaffold

## Purpose

The frontend layer has two experiences:

- user app for markets, deposits, switches, claims, portfolio, and Base Sepolia faucet support
- operator app for health, keeper schedule, oracle state, incident response, and prepared governance actions

Both apps use the shared ABI/address registry in [`../abi-map.md`](../abi-map.md).

## Data Model

Default UI data flow:

1. API serves indexed PostgreSQL state.
2. WebSocket pushes indexed updates.
3. Wallet submits user transactions directly to chain.
4. UI waits for indexed confirmation and shows data freshness.

Direct chain reads:

- user app: only for wallet simulation and allowance/balance checks
- operator app: only through explicit live refresh or transaction preparation

## Shared Frontend Packages

Future implementation should isolate:

- `contracts`: viem/wagmi contract configs from registry
- `api`: typed REST client
- `ws`: reconnecting WebSocket client
- `format`: e8 price formatting, token amount formatting, enum labels
- `market-types`: labels and compatibility rules from `currentSmartContract.md`
- `tx`: transaction simulation, wallet submit, indexed confirmation tracking
- `env`: environment and chain config

## Contract Config

Frontend should generate contract config from the registry:

- `marketEngine`: proxy address plus `IMarketEngine` ABI
- `dispatcher`: proxy address plus `MarketEngineDispatcher` ABI for operator-only screens
- `stakeToken`: Base Sepolia mock ERC20 address plus token ABI
- `faucet`: Base Sepolia faucet address plus faucet ABI

Do not hardcode implementation or module addresses into user transaction code.

## UX State Rules

- Show `globalPaused` prominently.
- Show stale indexed data with `lastSyncAt`.
- Show rolling halted state before any deposit/switch action.
- Show oracle and resolver labels for every market.
- Show claimable/refund states from indexed state and position view.
- For Base Sepolia, show faucet tooling only when `chainId == 84532`.

## User and Operator Split

The user app should not expose privileged controls.

The operator app should not hide the operational consequences of actions:

- every prepared transaction shows required role
- every action links to runbook guidance
- every critical state displays the exact getter or event source
- production actions are flagged as Safe/governance-required

# Pipeline Architecture Scaffold

## Purpose

The pipeline turns chain events into indexed state, schedules keeper work, tracks oracle health, and opens operator incidents. It follows the public-RPC optimized architecture in [../.tecStackPublicRPC.md](../.tecStackPublicRPC.md).

## Services

| Service | Responsibility | RPC policy |
|---|---|---|
| `retropick-index` | Batched log indexing, state projection, reorg handling | `eth_getLogs` batched, `eth_blockNumber`, rare header reads for reorgs |
| `retropick-keeper` | Execute scheduled lifecycle jobs | PG-driven idle loop, one live chain preflight per execution |
| `retropick-alert` | Incidents, alert routing, oracle stale checks | PostgreSQL only in normal operation |
| `retropick-reporter` | TrustedReporter signing and posting | Only for reporter-enabled templates |

The old idle oracle polling service should not be implemented. Oracle health comes from indexed Chainlink feed events and `oracle_health` rows.

## Indexer Inputs

Contract log sources:

- MarketEngine proxy with `MarketEngineDispatcher` ABI
- TrustedReporter adapter if deployed/configured
- TokenFaucet on Base Sepolia
- MockERC20 stake token on Base Sepolia
- Chainlink feed proxy addresses listed in `feed_registry`

Do not index module addresses for normal protocol state. Modules are routing targets, not the user-facing event source.

## MarketEngine Event Map

| Event group | Events | Projection target |
|---|---|---|
| Template | `TemplateUpserted`, `MarketInitialized` | `templates`, `audit_log` |
| Epoch lifecycle | `EpochOpened`, `EpochLocked`, `EpochLockedV2`, `EpochResolved`, `EpochResolvedV2`, `EpochCancelled` | `epochs`, `keeper_schedule`, `chain_events` |
| User positions | `PositionDeposited`, `SideSwitched`, `Claimed`, `UserEpochIndexed` | `positions`, `user_epochs`, `epochs` |
| Rolling | `RollingGenesisStarted`, `RollingGenesisLocked`, `RollingRoundExecuted`, `RollingHalted`, `RollingLifecycleReset` | `ledgers`, `epochs`, `keeper_schedule`, `incidents` |
| Yield/recovery | `YieldRouterSet`, `YieldRouterDisabled`, `YieldRouterFailureRecorded`, `YieldEmergencyWithdrawn`, `EpochYieldAccrued`, routed-claims events | `operator_state`, `epochs`, `incidents`, `audit_log` |
| Governance | `Upgraded`, module events, selector events, oracle setter events, role updates | `audit_log`, `incidents` |
| Fees/LM | `FeesWithdrawn`, `LMRewardReceived`, `LMRewardsEnabledUpdated` | `audit_log`, `operator_state` |

## Reporter Event Map

TrustedReporter events should populate oracle/reporter audit state:

- `ResultPosted`
- `LockSamplePosted`
- `OhlcPosted`
- `ResolveResultCleared`
- `LockSampleCleared`
- `OhlcResultCleared`
- `TrustedReporterUpdated`
- `MaxSignatureAgeUpdated`
- ownership events

Reporter incidents should link market ID to `positionKey(templateId, epochId)` where applicable.

## Chainlink Feed Event Map

Index Chainlink `AnswerUpdated(int256 current, uint256 roundId, uint256 updatedAt)` from active feed proxies.

Projection:

- `oracle_readings`
- `oracle_health`
- `feed_registry.last_healthy_at`
- `keeper_schedule` preflight context
- `ops:oracle` WebSocket notifications

Do not call every adapter every minute for feed freshness. The alert service can compute staleness from indexed feed events.

## Keeper Scheduler

Schedule jobs from indexed events:

- after `EpochOpened`: schedule `lockEpoch`
- after `EpochLocked`: schedule `resolveEpoch`
- after `RollingGenesisStarted`: schedule `genesisLockRolling`
- after `RollingGenesisLocked`: schedule `executeRollingRound`
- after `RollingRoundExecuted`: schedule next `executeRollingRound`
- after halt/cancel/reset events: update or disable affected jobs

Keeper job fields:

- `id`
- `template_id`
- `epoch_id`
- `action`
- `scheduled_at`
- `window_end_at`
- `status`
- `attempt_count`
- `last_error`
- `tx_hash`
- `preflight_snapshot`

## Keeper Execution Rule

Before broadcasting:

1. lock the job row with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`
2. record an execution attempt
3. validate PG projected state
4. perform one live chain read for the minimum required state
5. build/sign/send transaction
6. wait for receipt with backoff
7. write receipt and post-state validation

Never run an idle loop that calls `eth_call` every few seconds.

## Reorg Handling

Indexer must store:

- block number
- block hash
- parent hash if available
- log index
- transaction hash
- removed flag

On suspected reorg:

1. stop applying new projections
2. locate common ancestor within configured depth
3. roll back affected projections or rebuild from canonical event log rows
4. re-apply canonical logs
5. emit an incident if depth exceeds threshold

## Core Tables

Minimum schema ownership:

- `chain_events`
- `indexer_state`
- `contracts`
- `templates`
- `ledgers`
- `epochs`
- `positions`
- `user_epochs`
- `oracle_readings`
- `oracle_health`
- `feed_registry`
- `keeper_schedule`
- `keeper_executions`
- `incidents`
- `audit_log`

## Public RPC Policy

Default endpoint order for Base mainnet profile:

- `https://mainnet.base.org`
- `https://base.llamarpc.com`
- `https://1rpc.io/base`
- `https://base-mainnet.public.blastapi.io`
- `https://base.rpc.thirdweb.com`

Base Sepolia should use equivalent public or configured testnet endpoints from environment config.

RPC budget target:

- indexer: one batched `eth_getLogs` poll per interval
- keeper: one live read and one transaction path per actual execution
- API: zero routine chain calls
- alerting: zero routine chain calls

Paid RPC is added only after measured public endpoint error rate, latency, or scale requires it.

## Alert Rules

Open or update incidents for:

- rolling halt
- keeper missed or nearly missed window
- keeper tx failure
- yield router disabled
- unreconciled recovered amount
- stale feed for active template
- unexpected implementation upgrade
- unexpected module/selector event
- oracle cursor reset
- reporter clear/rotation/post outside schedule

Every incident should link:

- environment
- chain id
- template id
- epoch id if applicable
- transaction hash
- event name
- decoded event payload
- runbook section

# RetroPick Protocol — Production-Grade VPS Stack Architecture

**Version:** 1.0  
**Author:** Senior Engineering Design  
**Date:** April 2026  
**Scope:** Full-stack production architecture — VPS, Go backend, PostgreSQL, event-driven pipeline, user frontend, operator dashboard, keeper automation, oracle monitoring, incident response infrastructure

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Philosophy and Design Constraints](#1-philosophy-and-design-constraints)
2. [System Overview](#2-system-overview)
3. [VPS Hardware and OS Layer](#3-vps-hardware-and-os-layer)
4. [PostgreSQL Schema — Single Database for Everything](#4-postgresql-schema--single-database-for-everything)
5. [Go Backend — API Server Architecture](#5-go-backend--api-server-architecture)
6. [Event-Driven Pipeline — Chain Indexer](#6-event-driven-pipeline--chain-indexer)
7. [Keeper Automation Service](#7-keeper-automation-service)
8. [Oracle Monitor Service](#8-oracle-monitor-service)
9. [TrustedReporter Service](#9-trustedreporter-service)
10. [User Frontend — Next.js](#10-user-frontend--nextjs)
11. [Operator Dashboard — Internal](#11-operator-dashboard--internal)
12. [Notification and Alerting Pipeline](#12-notification-and-alerting-pipeline)
13. [Authentication and Session Management](#13-authentication-and-session-management)
14. [Nginx Reverse Proxy and TLS](#14-nginx-reverse-proxy-and-tls)
15. [Process Management and Service Topology](#15-process-management-and-service-topology)
16. [Backup, Recovery, and WAL Archiving](#16-backup-recovery-and-wal-archiving)
17. [CI/CD Pipeline](#17-cicd-pipeline)
18. [Security Hardening](#18-security-hardening)
19. [Observability Stack — Logs, Metrics, Traces](#19-observability-stack--logs-metrics-traces)
20. [Incident Response Runbooks](#20-incident-response-runbooks)
21. [Deployment Checklist — Mainnet Go-Live](#21-deployment-checklist--mainnet-go-live)
22. [Cost Model and Scaling Thresholds](#22-cost-model-and-scaling-thresholds)

---

## 1. Philosophy and Design Constraints

### 1.1 Core Engineering Philosophy

This is a **lean, boring-stack, production-first architecture**. The prediction market protocol
is complex enough at the smart contract layer — the infrastructure must be simple, observable,
and recoverable without heroics.

Guiding principles, in priority order:

1. **Correctness over cleverness.** A keeper that misses an epoch is worse than an ugly Go function.
2. **PostgreSQL for everything.** One database. No Redis, no Kafka, no Elasticsearch unless
   PostgreSQL genuinely cannot do the job. It can. LISTEN/NOTIFY replaces most message queues
   at this scale. `SKIP LOCKED` queues replace job runners.
3. **Single VPS until it cracks.** A single well-tuned VPS with PostgreSQL on a Unix socket
   is faster than an RDS instance behind a NAT gateway. Add the second server when the first
   one runs out of CPU, not because someone said "microservices".
4. **Go for the backend.** Statically compiled, single binary per service, trivial to deploy,
   goroutine concurrency maps directly to the event-driven workload.
5. **Every state change is auditable.** The prediction market runs real money. Every operator
   action, every keeper call, every oracle read, every epoch transition must produce a
   durable log row in PostgreSQL before the on-chain transaction is broadcast.
6. **Fail loudly, recover explicitly.** The runbook from the smart contract Operator Runbook
   applies equally to this layer. Pause first, inspect, then recover. No silent retries.

### 1.2 What the Stack Must Support

Derived from the smart contract documentation:

**Chain-facing requirements:**
- Index all MarketEngine events in real time (EpochOpened, EpochLocked, EpochResolved,
  RollingHalted, YieldRouterDisabled, etc.)
- Execute keeper calls: `executeRollingRound`, `lockEpoch`, `resolveEpoch`, with precise
  timing windows and buffer enforcement
- Monitor Chainlink oracle feed freshness per template before every keeper call
- Support TrustedReporter signature generation and posting
- Support emergency pause, recovery, and reconciliation flows

**User-facing requirements:**
- Wallet-connected deposits, switches, claims
- Real-time market state (pool sizes, current price, time to lock/resolve)
- Historical epoch results and personal position history
- WebSocket feed for live price ticks and pool updates
- Position view: getUserEpochs pagination, per-epoch claim status

**Operator-facing requirements:**
- Full protocol state dashboard: globalPaused, yieldRouterDisabled, activeEpochIds,
  unreconciledRecoveredAmount per template
- Template management: upsert, initialize, configure
- Keeper health: last execution, next window, halt reason
- Alert management and incident tracking
- Fee withdrawal interface

---

## 2. System Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         SINGLE VPS (Hetzner CX52)                       │
│                                                                          │
│  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Nginx + TLS   │  │  Nginx + TLS   │  │    Nginx + TLS           │   │
│  │  app.retropick │  │  ops.retropick │  │    api.retropick         │   │
│  └───────┬────────┘  └───────┬────────┘  └────────────┬─────────────┘   │
│          │                   │                        │                  │
│  ┌───────▼────────┐  ┌───────▼────────┐  ┌───────────▼─────────────┐   │
│  │  User Frontend │  │  Operator Dash │  │     API Server (Go)      │   │
│  │  Next.js :3000 │  │  Next.js :3001 │  │     retropick-api :8080  │   │
│  └────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │     - REST endpoints     │   │

### 2.1 Service Inventory

| Service | Binary | Port | Purpose |
|---------|--------|------|---------|
| `retropick-api` | Go | 8080 | REST + WebSocket API for user and operator frontends |
| `retropick-index` | Go | 8081 (internal) | Block-by-block event indexer from Base L2 |
| `retropick-keeper` | Go | 8082 (internal) | Scheduled epoch lifecycle automation |
| `retropick-oracle` | Go | 8083 (internal) | Chainlink feed freshness monitor |
| `retropick-reporter` | Go | 8084 (internal) | TrustedReporter EIP-712 signer |
| `retropick-alert` | Go | 8085 (internal) | Notification dispatcher (PagerDuty/Telegram/email) |
| `nginx` | system | 80/443 | Reverse proxy, TLS termination |
| `postgresql` | system | 5432 (Unix socket) | Primary database |
| `app-frontend` | Node | 3000 | User-facing Next.js |
| `ops-frontend` | Node | 3001 | Operator dashboard Next.js |

All Go services run as `systemd` units. PostgreSQL listens on Unix socket only — no TCP exposure.

## 3. VPS Hardware and OS Layer

### 3.1 Server Specification

**Provider:** Hetzner Cloud (cheapest reliable provider with European data center)  
**Initial tier:** CX32 (4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 80 GB NVMe) — ~€11/month  
**Scale tier:** CX52 (8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 240 GB NVMe) — ~€38/month

**Why Hetzner over DigitalOcean or Linode:** 4× cheaper per core, better NVMe I/O,
same network quality. Base L2 RPC calls are outbound-only so datacenter location matters
minimally.

**Additional volume:** 200 GB detached block storage for PostgreSQL WAL archive — ~€9.20/month  
**Snapshot:** weekly automated VPS snapshot — ~€2/month  
**Total infrastructure cost:** ~€55/month at production scale

## 4. PostgreSQL Schema — Single Database for Everything

### 4.1 Database Layout

```sql
-- Three logical databases, all on the same PostgreSQL instance
-- connected via Unix socket for zero-latency access

CREATE DATABASE retropick_main;   -- market state, positions, epochs
CREATE DATABASE retropick_ops;    -- operator actions, keeper logs, incidents
CREATE DATABASE retropick_audit;  -- immutable append-only audit trail
```

### 4.2 PostgreSQL Configuration (`postgresql.conf`)

```ini
# Performance tuning for 8GB RAM VPS
shared_buffers = 2GB                    # 25% of RAM
effective_cache_size = 6GB             # 75% of RAM
work_mem = 16MB                        # per sort/hash operation
maintenance_work_mem = 512MB           # for VACUUM, index builds
max_connections = 200                  # Go services use pgx pool
min_wal_size = 512MB
max_wal_size = 4GB
wal_level = replica                    # required for WAL archiving
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'cp %p /mnt/wal-archive/%f'
checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9
random_page_cost = 1.1                 # NVMe SSD — sequential ≈ random
effective_io_concurrency = 200        # NVMe parallelism
default_statistics_target = 100
wal_buffers = 64MB
synchronous_commit = on               # correctness over speed for financial data
fsync = on                            # never disable on a financial system

# Connection pooling via PgBouncer (transaction mode)
# Go services connect to PgBouncer on Unix socket
# PgBouncer connects to PostgreSQL on Unix socket

# LISTEN/NOTIFY for internal pub/sub
# Used by indexer → api-server for real-time updates
```

### 4.4 Core Schema — `retropick_main`

```sql
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- TEMPLATES
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TYPE execution_mode AS ENUM ('manual', 'rolling');
CREATE TYPE oracle_kind AS ENUM ('chainlink', 'trusted_reporter');
CREATE TYPE oracle_class AS ENUM (
  'chainlink_price', 'chainlink_rate', 'chainlink_smartdata',
  'chainlink_macro', 'chainlink_equity'
);
CREATE TYPE market_type AS ENUM (
  'direction', 'threshold', 'range_close', 'velocity',
  'ladder', 'convergence', 'composite', 'corridor', 'cascade'
);
CREATE TYPE rolling_phase AS ENUM (
  'uninitialized', 'genesis_open', 'live', 'halted'
);
CREATE TYPE rolling_halt_reason AS ENUM (
  'none', 'buffer_miss_on_lock', 'buffer_miss_on_resolve',
  'oracle_failure', 'oracle_confidence_wide', 'manual_admin'
);
CREATE TYPE epoch_status AS ENUM (
  'scheduled', 'open', 'locked', 'resolved', 'cancelled', 'voided'
);

CREATE TABLE templates (
  template_id          BYTEA PRIMARY KEY,           -- keccak256(slug)
  slug                 VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  asset_symbol         VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
  market_type          market_type NOT NULL,
  execution_mode       execution_mode NOT NULL,
  oracle_kind          oracle_kind NOT NULL,
  oracle_class         oracle_class,
  oracle_feed_id       BYTEA,                        -- Chainlink proxy address as bytes32
  event_oracle_address VARCHAR(42),                 -- TrustedReporter adapter address
  absolute_threshold_e8 NUMERIC(38, 0),
  range_bounds_e8      NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  velocity_bounds_e4   NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  ladder_bounds_e8     NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  ladder_payout_weights_bps INT[],
  oracle_feed_id_b     BYTEA,                        -- Convergence second feed
  spread_tolerance_bps INT,
  composite_feed_ids   BYTEA[],
  composite_conditions SMALLINT[],
  composite_feed_count SMALLINT,
  composite_logic      VARCHAR(16),                 -- 'and'|'or'|'majority'
  composite_thresholds_e8 NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  cascade_downward     BOOLEAN,
  anchor_price_e8      NUMERIC(38, 0),
  rolling_interval_sec INT,
  rolling_buffer_sec   INT,
  switch_fee_bps       INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  settlement_fee_bps   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,
  oracle_max_delay_sec INT,
  oracle_max_conf_bps  INT,
  outcome_count        SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 2,
  is_active            BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  initialized          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LEDGERS (per-template rolling lifecycle state)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE ledgers (
  template_id              BYTEA PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES templates(template_id),
  active_epoch_id          BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_resolved_epoch_id   BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  rolling_phase            rolling_phase NOT NULL DEFAULT 'uninitialized',
  rolling_halt_reason      rolling_halt_reason NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
  rolling_next_epoch_id    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  halted_at_epoch_id       BIGINT,
  fee_reserve_total        NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  claims_reserve_total     NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  active_collateral_total  NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_routed_principal   NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  unreconciled_recovered   NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_sync_block          BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  updated_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- EPOCHS
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE epochs (
  template_id              BYTEA NOT NULL REFERENCES templates(template_id),
  epoch_id                 BIGINT NOT NULL,
  status                   epoch_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  open_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  lock_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  resolve_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  -- oracle checkpoints
  checkpoint_a_value_e8    NUMERIC(38, 0),
  checkpoint_a_publish_time TIMESTAMPTZ,
  checkpoint_a_oracle_round BIGINT,
  checkpoint_b_value_e8    NUMERIC(38, 0),
  checkpoint_b_publish_time TIMESTAMPTZ,
  checkpoint_b_oracle_round BIGINT,
  -- convergence second feed
  checkpoint_a_b_value_e8  NUMERIC(38, 0),
  checkpoint_b_b_value_e8  NUMERIC(38, 0),
  -- composite per-feed checkpoints (max 4 feeds)
  composite_a_values_e8    NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  composite_b_values_e8    NUMERIC(38, 0)[],
  -- OHLC for Corridor/Cascade
  epoch_high_e8            NUMERIC(38, 0),
  epoch_low_e8             NUMERIC(38, 0),
  ohlc_written             BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  -- pool accounting
  outcome_pools            NUMERIC(38, 0)[] NOT NULL,
  total_pool               NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- settlement outputs
  winning_outcome_mask     INT,
  claim_liability_total    NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  settlement_fee_total     NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  claimed_total            NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ref_mode                 BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  claimable                BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  remaining_winning_stake  NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  routed_principal         NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- on-chain identifiers
  open_tx_hash             VARCHAR(66),
  lock_tx_hash             VARCHAR(66),
  resolve_tx_hash          VARCHAR(66),
  cancel_tx_hash           VARCHAR(66),
  sync_block               BIGINT,
  created_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (template_id, epoch_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_epochs_status ON epochs(status) WHERE status IN ('open','locked');
CREATE INDEX idx_epochs_resolve_at ON epochs(resolve_at) WHERE status = 'locked';
CREATE INDEX idx_epochs_lock_at ON epochs(lock_at) WHERE status = 'open';
CREATE INDEX idx_epochs_claimable ON epochs(claimable) WHERE claimable = TRUE;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- POSITIONS (user deposits per epoch)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE positions (
  template_id   BYTEA NOT NULL,
  epoch_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
  user_address  VARCHAR(42) NOT NULL,
  stakes        NUMERIC(38, 0)[] NOT NULL,   -- per outcome
  total_stake   NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  claimed       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  claimed_amount NUMERIC(38, 0),
  claim_tx_hash VARCHAR(66),
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (template_id, epoch_id, user_address),
  FOREIGN KEY (template_id, epoch_id) REFERENCES epochs(template_id, epoch_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_positions_user ON positions(user_address);
CREATE INDEX idx_positions_unclaimed ON positions(user_address, claimable)
  WHERE claimed = FALSE;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- ORACLE READINGS (raw feed samples, for monitoring and audit)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE oracle_readings (
  id            BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  feed_id       BYTEA NOT NULL,
  adapter_class oracle_class NOT NULL,
  round_id      BIGINT,
  price_e8      NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL,
  confidence_e8 NUMERIC(38, 0) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  publish_time  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  sampled_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  sampled_by    VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,             -- 'keeper'|'oracle_monitor'
  is_stale      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  staleness_sec INT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_oracle_readings_feed ON oracle_readings(feed_id, sampled_at DESC);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- CHAIN EVENTS (raw indexed events from Base L2)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE chain_events (
  id             BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  block_number   BIGINT NOT NULL,
  tx_hash        VARCHAR(66) NOT NULL,
  log_index      INT NOT NULL,
  contract_addr  VARCHAR(42) NOT NULL,
  event_name     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  template_id    BYTEA,
  epoch_id       BIGINT,
  user_address   VARCHAR(42),
  payload        JSONB NOT NULL,
  indexed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE (tx_hash, log_index)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_chain_events_template ON chain_events(template_id, block_number DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_chain_events_block ON chain_events(block_number DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_chain_events_name ON chain_events(event_name, indexed_at DESC);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- INDEXER CURSOR (tracks indexing progress)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE indexer_state (
  id              INT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1,
  last_block      BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_block_hash VARCHAR(66),
  last_indexed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  reorg_depth     INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  CHECK (id = 1)   -- singleton row
);

INSERT INTO indexer_state DEFAULT VALUES;

-- NOTIFY channel used by indexer to push real-time updates to API server
-- PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY replaces Redis pub/sub for this use case

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- WEBSOCKET SESSION STATE (stored in PG, not in-memory)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE ws_subscriptions (
  session_id    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_address  VARCHAR(42),
  subscriptions JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  connected_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_ping     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  server_id     VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL   -- for future multi-server support
);
```

### 4.5 Schema — `retropick_ops`

```sql
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- KEEPER EXECUTION LOG
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TYPE keeper_action AS ENUM (
  'genesis_start_rolling', 'genesis_lock_rolling', 'execute_rolling_round',
  'open_epoch', 'lock_epoch', 'resolve_epoch', 'cancel_epoch',
  'halt_rolling_market', 'cancel_rolling_epoch_while_halted',
  'reset_rolling_lifecycle', 'pause_program', 'unpause_program',
  'yield_emergency_withdraw', 'reconcile_routed_principal',
  'withdraw_fees', 'reset_oracle_cursor', 'set_yield_router',
  'upsert_template', 'initialize_market'
);

CREATE TYPE keeper_result AS ENUM ('success', 'failed', 'reverted', 'skipped');

CREATE TABLE keeper_executions (
  id             BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  action         keeper_action NOT NULL,
  template_id    BYTEA,
  epoch_id       BIGINT,
  result         keeper_result NOT NULL,
  tx_hash        VARCHAR(66),
  block_number   BIGINT,
  gas_used       BIGINT,
  gas_price_gwei NUMERIC(20, 9),
  error_message  TEXT,
  pre_state      JSONB,   -- snapshot of relevant state before execution
  post_state     JSONB,   -- snapshot after execution
  executed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  executed_by    VARCHAR(42) NOT NULL   -- sender address
);

CREATE INDEX idx_keeper_executions_template ON keeper_executions(template_id, executed_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_keeper_executions_result ON keeper_executions(result) WHERE result != 'success';

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- KEEPER SCHEDULE (what the keeper intends to do and when)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TYPE schedule_status AS ENUM ('pending', 'executing', 'done', 'failed', 'cancelled');

CREATE TABLE keeper_schedule (
  id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  template_id     BYTEA NOT NULL,
  epoch_id        BIGINT,
  action          keeper_action NOT NULL,
  scheduled_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  window_end_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,   -- buffer deadline
  status          schedule_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  execution_id    BIGINT REFERENCES keeper_executions(id),
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- SKIP LOCKED pattern: keeper SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
-- picks next pending job atomically without a separate queue service
CREATE INDEX idx_keeper_schedule_pending ON keeper_schedule(scheduled_at)
  WHERE status = 'pending';

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- ORACLE HEALTH TRACKING
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE oracle_health (
  feed_id         BYTEA PRIMARY KEY,
  adapter_class   oracle_class NOT NULL,
  last_price_e8   NUMERIC(38, 0),
  last_round_id   BIGINT,
  last_updated    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_checked    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  is_stale        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  staleness_sec   INT,
  heartbeat_sec   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3600,
  alert_sent      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  alert_sent_at   TIMESTAMPTZ
);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- INCIDENTS
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TYPE incident_severity AS ENUM ('critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low');
CREATE TYPE incident_status AS ENUM ('open', 'investigating', 'mitigating', 'resolved');

CREATE TABLE incidents (
  id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  title       VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  severity    incident_severity NOT NULL,
  status      incident_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  template_id BYTEA,
  epoch_id    BIGINT,
  triggered_by VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,   -- 'oracle_monitor'|'keeper'|'indexer'|'manual'
  alert_payload JSONB,
  opened_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  resolved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  resolved_by VARCHAR(42),
  resolution  TEXT,
  timeline    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'
);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- OPERATOR SESSIONS (admin auth)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE operator_sessions (
  session_id   UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  operator_addr VARCHAR(42) NOT NULL,
  siwe_nonce   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  siwe_message TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  revoked      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE
);

CREATE INDEX idx_operator_sessions_addr ON operator_sessions(operator_addr)
  WHERE revoked = FALSE;
```

## 6. Event-Driven Pipeline — Chain Indexer

### 6.1 Architecture

The indexer is a separate Go binary (`retropick-index`) that subscribes to Base L2
event logs, decodes them, writes to PostgreSQL, and emits NOTIFY signals to the
API server.

```
Base L2 Node (Alchemy)
        │
        │ eth_getLogs (poll every 2s)
        │ + eth_subscribe newHeads (WebSocket)
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    retropick-index (Go)                               │
│                                                                       │
│  ┌─────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐   │
│  │  Block Fetcher  │──▶│  Event Decoder  │──▶│  State Updater   │   │
│  │  (RPC poller)   │   │  (ABI decode)   │   │  (PG writer)     │   │
│  └─────────────────┘   └─────────────────┘   └────────┬─────────┘   │
│                                                        │              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────▼──────────┐  │
│  │  Reorg Handler — detects chain reorgs, rolls back PG state     │  │
│  │  (keep 64-block buffer, compare block hashes)                  │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                        │              │
│                               pg_notify('market_update', payload)     │
│                               pg_notify('keeper_alert', payload)      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
PostgreSQL (chain_events, epochs, positions, ledgers)
        │
        │ NOTIFY
        ▼
retropick-api (WebSocket hub fan-out)
```

### 6.2 Events Indexed (from MarketEngine)

| Event | Action |
|-------|--------|
| `EpochOpened(templateId, epochId, openAt, lockAt, resolveAt)` | INSERT epoch row, UPDATE ledger.activeEpochId, schedule keeper lock action |
| `EpochLocked(templateId, epochId)` / `EpochLockedV2(...)` | UPDATE epoch status→locked, write checkpointA, schedule keeper resolve action |
| `EpochResolved(templateId, epochId)` / `EpochResolvedV2(...)` | UPDATE epoch status→resolved, write checkpointB + settlement outputs, set claimable=true |
| `EpochCancelled(templateId, epochId, reason, voided)` | UPDATE epoch status→cancelled/voided, set refundMode |
| `PositionDeposited(templateId, epochId, user, outcomeIdx, amount)` | UPSERT position, UPDATE epoch outcome_pools, notify pool_update |
| `PositionSwitched(...)` | UPDATE position stakes, UPDATE epoch pools |
| `Claimed(templateId, epochId, user, amount)` | UPDATE position.claimed=true, UPDATE epoch.claimed_total |
| `RollingRoundExecuted(templateId, prev, cur, next)` | Cascade UPDATE for prev→resolved, cur→locked, next→open |
| `RollingHalted(templateId, reason, atEpoch)` | UPDATE ledger rolling_phase→halted, notify keeper_alert |
| `YieldRouterDisabled(templateId)` | UPDATE global state, notify keeper_alert CRITICAL |
| `YieldEmergencyWithdrawn(templateId, amount)` | UPDATE ledger unreconciled_recovered, open incident |
| `OracleCursorReset(templateId, feedId)` | Audit log INSERT, notify ops |
| `ModuleRegistered/Revoked/SelectorSet` | Audit log INSERT, notify ops CRITICAL |
| `FeesWithdrawn(templateId, amount)` | UPDATE ledger.fee_reserve_total |

### 6.3 Reorg Safety

```go
// Indexer maintains a 64-block rolling buffer of block hashes.
// On each new block:
// 1. Check if parent hash matches the last indexed block hash.
// 2. If mismatch: reorg detected.
//    a. Walk back to the common ancestor (max 64 blocks).
//    b. DELETE chain_events with block_number > ancestor.
//    c. Re-apply events from the fork block.
//    d. UPDATE indexer_state.reorg_depth.
// 3. If reorg depth > 20 blocks: CRITICAL alert, pause indexer, human review.

// For financial correctness: all epoch state writes in a single PG transaction
// per block. If PG write fails, the block is retried up to 3 times before alert.
```

## 7. Keeper Automation Service

### 7.1 Keeper Architecture

The keeper (`retropick-keeper`) is the most safety-critical service. It executes
on-chain transactions. Every execution is pre-validated, logged before broadcast,
and post-validated.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     retropick-keeper (Go)                             │
│                                                                       │
│  ┌─────────────────┐                                                  │
│  │  Schedule Poller│  SELECT * FROM keeper_schedule                   │
│  │  (5-second tick)│  WHERE status='pending'                          │
│  │                 │  AND scheduled_at <= NOW()                       │
│  │                 │  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED                          │
│  │                 │  LIMIT 1                                         │
│  └────────┬────────┘                                                  │
│           │                                                           │
│  ┌────────▼────────┐                                                  │
│  │ Pre-flight Check│  For each action:                                │
│  │                 │  1. Read live contract state (chain call)        │
│  │                 │  2. Verify action is still valid                 │
│  │                 │  3. Check oracle freshness                       │
│  │                 │  4. Check buffer window still open               │
│  │                 │  5. Check protocol not paused                    │
│  └────────┬────────┘                                                  │
│           │ passes                                                    │
│  ┌────────▼────────┐                                                  │
│  │  Transaction    │  1. INSERT keeper_executions (pre_state, pending)│
│  │  Builder        │  2. Estimate gas + sanity check                  │
│  │                 │  3. Sign transaction (keeper private key)        │
│  │                 │  4. Broadcast to Base L2                        │
│  │                 │  5. Wait for receipt (timeout: 60s)              │
│  │                 │  6. UPDATE keeper_executions (result, tx_hash)   │
│  │                 │  7. Verify post-state via chain read             │
│  └────────┬────────┘                                                  │
│           │                                                           │
│  ┌────────▼────────┐                                                  │
│  │  Post-Exec      │  On success: schedule next action for template   │
│  │  Handler        │  On failure: classify error, alert, open incident│
│  └─────────────────┘                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 7.2 Keeper Pre-flight Checks (Per Action Type)

```go
// executeRollingRound pre-flight:
type RollingRoundPreflight struct {
    rollingPhase     string        // must be "live"
    globalPaused     bool          // must be false
    resolveWindow    TimeWindow    // now >= prev.resolveAt
    lockWindow       TimeWindow    // now >= cur.lockAt
    resolveBuffer    time.Duration // now <= prev.resolveAt + bufferSeconds
    lockBuffer       time.Duration // now <= cur.lockAt + bufferSeconds
    oracleFresh      bool          // feed updatedAt within maxDelaySeconds
    routerHealthy    bool          // !yieldRouterDisabled
    noUnreconciledRecovery bool    // totalUnreconciledRecovered == 0
    bufferPressure   float64       // percentage of buffer remaining (alert if < 25%)
}

// Fail-safe: if any preflight fails, the action is:
// 1. Marked as 'skipped' in keeper_schedule
// 2. An alert is emitted if buffer pressure is < 25% remaining
// 3. An incident is opened if buffer is expired (miss is imminent)
// Never retried blindly. Operator must intervene.
```

### 7.3 Keeper Schedule Builder

```go
// After EpochOpened event:
// INSERT INTO keeper_schedule:
//   action=lock_epoch, scheduled_at=lockAt, window_end_at=lockAt+bufferSeconds

// After EpochLocked event:
// INSERT INTO keeper_schedule:
//   action=resolve_epoch, scheduled_at=resolveAt, window_end_at=resolveAt+bufferSeconds

// After RollingRoundExecuted event:
// The next round's resolve and lock windows are derived from the new epoch's timings
// INSERT INTO keeper_schedule:
//   action=execute_rolling_round, scheduled_at=new_lockAt, window_end_at=new_lockAt+bufferSeconds

// Buffer pressure alerting:
// Poll keeper_schedule every 60 seconds
// For any pending action: if (window_end_at - NOW()) < 0.25 * bufferSeconds → WARN alert
// For any pending action: if (window_end_at - NOW()) < 0     → CRITICAL alert + incident
```

### 7.4 Gas Price Strategy

```go
// Base L2 (OP Stack): EIP-1559 base fee + priority fee
// Strategy: use eth_gasPrice or eth_feeHistory for base fee estimate
// Priority fee: 0.001 gwei (Base L2 is very cheap)
// Gas multiplier: 1.2x estimated gas as limit
// Resubmit if not mined within 30s: bump priority fee by 50%
// Max resubmit attempts: 3
// If still not mined after 3 attempts: alert + mark as failed
// Never use high gas price automatically — require operator approval above threshold

type GasConfig struct {
    MaxBaseFeeGwei    float64  // hard cap — default 0.1 gwei on Base L2
    PriorityFeeGwei   float64  // default 0.001 gwei
    GasLimitMultiplier float64 // default 1.2x estimate
    ResubmitAfterSec  int      // default 30s
    MaxResubmitCount  int      // default 3
}
```

## 9. TrustedReporter Service

### 9.1 Architecture

```go
// retropick-reporter: signs and posts TrustedReporter oracle data
// Used for: Corridor markets (OHLC), Cascade markets (OHLC),
//           and any Threshold market configured with TrustedReporter oracle kind

// Security model: private key stored in env var, NEVER in PostgreSQL
// All signed messages are logged to audit_log BEFORE posting to chain

type ReporterService struct {
    signerKey    *ecdsa.PrivateKey     // loaded from REPORTER_PRIVATE_KEY env
    adapterAddr  string
    pgConn       *pgxpool.Pool
    client       *ethclient.Client
    dataFetchers map[string]DataFetcher // marketId → data source
}

// Posting flow for a market resolution:
// 1. Fetch raw data from approved source (NOAA API, internal OHLC computation)
// 2. Validate data: range checks, source health checks
// 3. Compute EIP-712 typed data hash (matching TrustedReporterAdapter's domain)
// 4. Sign with private key
// 5. INSERT into audit_log (payload includes message hash, signer, data)
// 6. Call postResolveResult() or postOhlcResult() on TrustedReporterAdapter
// 7. Wait for on-chain confirmation
// 8. Mark resolution as posted in keeper_schedule

// Key management notes:
// - Reporter key is separate from keeper key
// - Reporter key has ZERO on-chain admin access
// - Rotate reporter key via setTrustedReporter (operator flow, not automated)
// - Alert immediately if reporter key signs anything outside normal schedule
```

## 12. Notification and Alerting Pipeline

### 12.1 Alert Dispatcher Service

```go
// retropick-alert: subscribes to PG NOTIFY channels and dispatches alerts

type AlertDispatcher struct {
    pgConn      *pgxpool.Pool
    pagerduty   PagerDutyClient   // for CRITICAL alerts (rolling halt, yield router disabled)
    telegram    TelegramClient    // for WARN alerts (buffer pressure, oracle staleness)
    email       SMTPClient        // for LOW severity (daily digest)
}

// Severity routing:
// CRITICAL: PagerDuty page + Telegram + open incident in DB
//   - RollingHalted
//   - YieldRouterDisabled
//   - ModuleRegistered/Revoked (governance alert)
//   - Buffer miss imminent (< 5 minutes to window close)
//   - Oracle staleness > maxDelaySec
//   - Chain reorg depth > 5

// HIGH: Telegram + open incident in DB
//   - Buffer pressure < 25% of window remaining
//   - Oracle staleness > 80% of maxDelaySec
//   - Keeper transaction failed
//   - YieldRouterFailureCount > 1

// MEDIUM: Telegram + DB log
//   - Keeper skipped action (pre-flight failed)
//   - Oracle confidence too wide
//   - Unexpected admin transaction from non-keeper address

// LOW: DB log only (aggregated in daily digest email)
//   - Successful fee withdrawal
//   - Oracle cursor reset
//   - Rolling lifecycle reset
```

### 13.1 User Auth — SIWE (Sign-In With Ethereum)

```go
// SIWE flow:
// 1. GET /api/v1/auth/nonce?address=0x... → returns random nonce, stored in PG
// 2. Frontend builds SIWE message:
//    domain: app.retropick.xyz
//    address: 0x...
//    statement: Sign in to RetroPick Protocol
//    nonce: <from server>
//    chainId: 8453 (Base)
//    expirationTime: now + 24h
// 3. User signs with wallet
// 4. POST /api/v1/auth/verify { message, signature }
//    Server: verifyMessage with siwe-go library
//    If valid: INSERT sessions row, return JWT (HS256, 24h expiry)
// 5. Subsequent requests: Authorization: Bearer <jwt>

// Session storage in PostgreSQL:
CREATE TABLE user_sessions (
  session_id   UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_address VARCHAR(42) NOT NULL,
  siwe_nonce   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  jwt_jti      UUID NOT NULL,            -- JWT ID for invalidation
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  last_seen    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  user_agent   TEXT,
  ip_address   INET
);

## 16. Backup, Recovery, and WAL Archiving

### 16.1 Backup Strategy

```bash
# Continuous WAL archiving to attached volume
# postgresql.conf: archive_command = 'cp %p /mnt/wal-archive/%f'
# This gives point-in-time recovery (PITR) to any point in the last 7 days

# Daily base backup with pg_basebackup
# /opt/retropick/scripts/backup.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR=/mnt/wal-archive/base_backups
DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

pg_basebackup \
  --pgdata="${BACKUP_DIR}/${DATE}" \
  --format=tar \
  --compress=9 \
  --checkpoint=fast \
  --progress

# Keep last 7 daily backups
find ${BACKUP_DIR} -maxdepth 1 -type d -mtime +7 -exec rm -rf {} +

# Upload to off-site (Cloudflare R2 or Hetzner Object Storage)
rclone sync ${BACKUP_DIR}/${DATE} r2:retropick-backups/${DATE}

echo "Backup completed: ${DATE}"
```

### 16.2 Recovery Time Objective (RTO)

| Scenario | RTO | Procedure |
|----------|-----|-----------|
| PostgreSQL crash (data intact) | < 1 minute | `systemctl restart postgresql` |
| Corrupt data file | < 30 minutes | PITR from WAL archive |
| VPS total loss | < 2 hours | New VPS + restore base backup + replay WAL |
| Catastrophic loss (all backups) | N/A — use chain as source of truth | Rebuild from chain events |

**Note on chain as ultimate truth:** The smart contract state is the canonical source.
If the PostgreSQL database is completely lost, the indexer can replay all events
from genesis block and rebuild the full state. This is the ultimate recovery path.
Estimated replay time from genesis: ~4 hours for 1 year of events.

## 17. CI/CD Pipeline

### 17.1 GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with: { go-version: '1.22' }
      - name: Run tests
        run: go test ./... -race -coverprofile=coverage.out
      - name: Check coverage
        run: go tool cover -func=coverage.out | grep total | awk '{if ($3+0 < 80) exit 1}'

  build:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build Go binaries
        run: |
          CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build \
            -ldflags="-s -w -X main.Version=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" \
            -o dist/retropick-api ./cmd/api
          # ... repeat for all services

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: binaries
          path: dist/

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production   # requires manual approval in GitHub
    steps:
      - name: Deploy binaries to VPS
        run: |
          # Copy binaries via scp
          scp dist/* retropick@${VPS_IP}:/opt/retropick/bin.new/

          # Run database migrations
          ssh retropick@${VPS_IP} "
            /opt/retropick/bin.new/retropick-api migrate up
          "

          # Atomic binary swap + restart (zero downtime for stateless services)
          ssh retropick@${VPS_IP} "
            mv /opt/retropick/bin.new /opt/retropick/bin.${DATE}
            ln -sfn /opt/retropick/bin.${DATE} /opt/retropick/bin
            systemctl restart retropick-api retropick-index retropick-keeper \
                             retropick-oracle retropick-reporter retropick-alert
          "

      - name: Health check
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -f https://api.retropick.xyz/api/v1/health

      - name: Rollback on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          ssh retropick@${VPS_IP} "
            ln -sfn /opt/retropick/bin.$(ls /opt/retropick/ | grep bin. | sort -r | head -2 | tail -1) \
              /opt/retropick/bin
            systemctl restart retropick-api retropick-index retropick-keeper
          "

### 18.2 Key Management

```
Keys in use:
1. Keeper private key (ECDSA secp256k1)
   - workerAuthority on the MarketEngine contract
   - Stored in /opt/retropick/config/keeper.env (600 permissions)
   - Holds minimal ETH (~0.05 ETH) — not a treasury key
   - If compromised: keeper can only call worker functions (no admin, no funds)
   - Rotation: update workerAuthority via admin Safe, then update env

2. Reporter private key (ECDSA secp256k1)
   - trustedReporter on TrustedReporterAdapter
   - Stored separately in /opt/retropick/config/reporter.env
   - Zero on-chain admin or fund access
   - Rotation: setTrustedReporter via admin Safe

3. Admin Safe (Gnosis Safe, 2-of-3 multisig)
   - All admin operations require multisig
   - Keys held by individual signers on hardware wallets
   - NEVER stored on the server
   - The server can PROPOSE transactions to the Safe but cannot execute alone

4. JWT signing secret
   - 256-bit random secret for user session JWTs
   - Stored in api.env
   - Rotation: all active sessions are invalidated when rotated
```

### 18.3 PostgreSQL Security

```sql
-- Application uses a single restricted role
CREATE ROLE retropick_app WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '${PG_PASSWORD}';

-- Explicit grants only

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO retropick_app;

-- Audit log: INSERT only
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log FROM retropick_app;

-- No DROP, no CREATE, no TRUNCATE
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM retropick_app;

-- PostgreSQL: no TCP access, Unix socket only
listen_addresses = ''   # disable TCP entirely

## 20. Incident Response Runbooks

### 20.1 RollingHalted Response

```
TRIGGER: RollingHalted event indexed / keeper_alert NOTIFY received
SEVERITY: HIGH

1. READ OPERATOR STATE
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OPS_TOKEN}" \
     https://ops.retropick.xyz/api/v1/ops/templates/{templateId}/state
   
   Capture: rollingHaltReason, haltedAtEpochId, activeEpochId

2. CLASSIFY HALT REASON
   - BufferMissOnLock / BufferMissOnResolve:
     * Was the keeper running? Check keeper logs
     * Was the oracle fresh at the time? Check oracle_health table
     * Was it a transient RPC issue?
   
   - OracleFailure:
     * Is the feed still stale now? Check oracle_health.is_stale
     * Is it a confidence issue? Check oracle_readings.confidence_e8
   
   - ManualAdmin: intentional halt, skip to step 5

3. IF ORACLE IS STILL STALE: WAIT
   Do not attempt recovery while the oracle is stale.
   Open incident. Monitor oracle health.
   Alert when oracle recovers.

4. IF ROOT CAUSE RESOLVED: PREPARE RECOVERY
   Via admin Safe (multisig):
   a. pauseProgram(true)
   b. cancelRollingEpochWhileHalted(templateId, haltedEpochId, reason, false)
   c. resetRollingLifecycle(templateId, nextEpochId)
   d. pauseProgram(false)
   
   Verify via: getOperatorTemplateView(templateId)
   Expected: rollingPhase=uninitialized, no stuck epochs

5. RESTART ROLLING
   Keeper will execute genesisStartRolling within 30 seconds of unpause.
   Monitor: watch keeper_schedule table and keeper_executions.

6. CONFIRM RECOVERY
   After 2 successful executeRollingRound calls: mark incident resolved.
```

### 20.2 YieldRouterDisabled Response

```
TRIGGER: YieldRouterDisabled event indexed
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — page immediately

This means 3 consecutive withdrawScaled failures occurred.
User deposits are no longer routing to Aave.
The protocol is NOT paused but is operating without yield.

1. DO NOT PANIC. User funds are safe. Markets continue to settle.
   The only impact: idle capital no longer earns yield.

2. INVESTIGATE:
   - Check Aave protocol status (status.aave.com)
   - Check YieldRouterV2 contract state
   - Read recent YieldRouterWithdrawFailed events from chain_events table
   - Check if failure was transient (Base sequencer issue?) or persistent

3. IF TRANSIENT (Aave/sequencer briefly unavailable):
   Via admin Safe:
   a. pauseProgram(true)
   b. resetYieldRouterFailures() -- only callable while paused
   c. pauseProgram(false)
   Monitor: next deposit should resume routing

4. IF PERSISTENT (Aave issue or router bug):
   a. Do NOT reset failures.
   b. Assess whether to deploy a new YieldRouterV2 or set router to address(0)
   c. Setting router to address(0) disables yield but markets continue safely
   d. Route: pauseProgram(true) → setYieldRouter(address(0), 0) → pauseProgram(false)

5. COMMUNICATE: Update incident notes with timeline.
```

### 22.1 Monthly Cost Breakdown

| Line Item | Cost |
|-----------|------|
| Hetzner CX32 VPS (4 vCPU, 8GB) | €11/month |
| Hetzner block storage 200GB (WAL archive) | €9.20/month |
| Weekly VPS snapshot | €2/month |
| Alchemy Base L2 RPC (free tier: 30M CU/month) | $0 |
| Let's Encrypt TLS | $0 |
| Cloudflare R2 backups (< 10GB/month) | $0 |
| PagerDuty (free tier) | $0 |
| Telegram Bot API | $0 |
| **Total Infrastructure** | **~€22/month** |

### 22.2 Scaling Thresholds

When to add resources:

| Metric | Scale Trigger | Action |
|--------|---------------|--------|
| CPU > 70% sustained | Add second VPS | Read replica for API, primary for indexer/keeper |
| PG connections > 150 | Increase PgBouncer pool | Bump default_pool_size from 20 to 40 |
| API p95 latency > 200ms | Profile + optimize | Check PG query plans, add indexes |
| WAL archive > 100GB/day | Increase volume | Hetzner volume is live-resizable |
| Chain indexer lag > 5 blocks sustained | Tune batch size | Increase getLogs batch from 100 to 500 blocks |
| Active WebSocket connections > 1000 | Add CDN WebSocket proxy | Cloudflare Durable Objects or Ably |

### 22.3 The Single-VPS Rule

**Do not add infrastructure because it feels more "production-grade."**
Add it when a specific metric exceeds a threshold.

At $22M/year volume with 0.3% protocol fee, revenue is ~$66,000/year.
The infrastructure cost at full single-VPS scale: ~€264/year.
That's 0.4% of revenue. The threshold for a second server is performance,
not aesthetics.

## Appendix B: Database Query Patterns

```sql
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Critical query: next scheduled keeper action (polled every 5s)
-- Must be sub-millisecond
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SELECT id, template_id, epoch_id, action, scheduled_at, window_end_at
FROM keeper_schedule
WHERE status = 'pending'
  AND scheduled_at <= NOW() + INTERVAL '10 seconds'
ORDER BY window_end_at ASC
LIMIT 1
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;

-- Index: idx_keeper_schedule_pending covers this exactly

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- User position query (portfolio page)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SELECT
  p.*,
  e.status,
  e.resolve_at,
  e.winning_outcome_mask,
  e.claimable,
  t.slug,
  t.asset_symbol,
  t.market_type
FROM positions p
JOIN epochs e ON (e.template_id, e.epoch_id) = (p.template_id, p.epoch_id)
JOIN templates t ON t.template_id = p.template_id
WHERE p.user_address = $1
  AND p.claimed = FALSE
ORDER BY e.resolve_at DESC
LIMIT 20 OFFSET $2;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Buffer pressure check (alert trigger, runs every 60s)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SELECT
  ks.template_id,
  ks.action,
  ks.scheduled_at,
  ks.window_end_at,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ks.window_end_at - NOW())) AS buffer_remaining_sec,
  t.rolling_buffer_sec,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ks.window_end_at - NOW())) / t.rolling_buffer_sec AS buffer_fraction
FROM keeper_schedule ks
JOIN templates t ON t.template_id = ks.template_id
WHERE ks.status = 'pending'
  AND EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ks.window_end_at - NOW())) / t.rolling_buffer_sec < 0.25
ORDER BY buffer_fraction ASC;
```

## 1. Philosophy and Design Constraints

### 1.1 Core Engineering Philosophy

This is a **lean, boring-stack, production-first architecture**. The prediction market protocol
is complex enough at the smart contract layer — the infrastructure must be simple, observable,
and recoverable without heroics.

Guiding principles, in priority order:

1. **Correctness over cleverness.** A keeper that misses an epoch is worse than an ugly Go function.
2. **PostgreSQL for everything.** One database. No Redis, no Kafka, no Elasticsearch unless
   PostgreSQL genuinely cannot do the job. It can. LISTEN/NOTIFY replaces most message queues
   at this scale. `SKIP LOCKED` queues replace job runners.
3. **Single VPS until it cracks.** A single well-tuned VPS with PostgreSQL on a Unix socket
   is faster than an RDS instance behind a NAT gateway. Add the second server when the first
   one runs out of CPU, not because someone said "microservices".
4. **Go for the backend.** Statically compiled, single binary per service, trivial to deploy,
   goroutine concurrency maps directly to the event-driven workload.
5. **Every state change is auditable.** The prediction market runs real money. Every operator
   action, every keeper call, every oracle read, every epoch transition must produce a
   durable log row in PostgreSQL before the on-chain transaction is broadcast.
6. **Fail loudly, recover explicitly.** The runbook from the smart contract Operator Runbook
   applies equally to this layer. Pause first, inspect, then recover. No silent retries.

### 1.2 What the Stack Must Support

Derived from the smart contract documentation:

**Chain-facing requirements:**
- Index all MarketEngine events in real time (EpochOpened, EpochLocked, EpochResolved,
  RollingHalted, YieldRouterDisabled, etc.)
- Execute keeper calls: `executeRollingRound`, `lockEpoch`, `resolveEpoch`, with precise
  timing windows and buffer enforcement
- Monitor Chainlink oracle feed freshness per template before every keeper call
- Support TrustedReporter signature generation and posting
- Support emergency pause, recovery, and reconciliation flows

**User-facing requirements:**
- Wallet-connected deposits, switches, claims
- Real-time market state (pool sizes, current price, time to lock/resolve)
- Historical epoch results and personal position history
- WebSocket feed for live price ticks and pool updates
- Position view: getUserEpochs pagination, per-epoch claim status

**Operator-facing requirements:**
- Full protocol state dashboard: globalPaused, yieldRouterDisabled, activeEpochIds,
  unreconciledRecoveredAmount per template
- Template management: upsert, initialize, configure
- Keeper health: last execution, next window, halt reason
- Alert management and incident tracking
- Fee withdrawal interface

## 3. VPS Hardware and OS Layer

### 3.1 Server Specification

**Provider:** Hetzner Cloud (cheapest reliable provider with European data center)  
**Initial tier:** CX32 (4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 80 GB NVMe) — ~€11/month  
**Scale tier:** CX52 (8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 240 GB NVMe) — ~€38/month

**Why Hetzner over DigitalOcean or Linode:** 4× cheaper per core, better NVMe I/O,
same network quality. Base L2 RPC calls are outbound-only so datacenter location matters
minimally.

**Additional volume:** 200 GB detached block storage for PostgreSQL WAL archive — ~€9.20/month  
**Snapshot:** weekly automated VPS snapshot — ~€2/month  
**Total infrastructure cost:** ~€55/month at production scale
